subject: Edge connectivity preflight and ops checkpoints
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@aldea.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge connectivity preflight and ops checkpoints

Hi Samir / Aldea ops team —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood Private for the Aldea edge footprint. Before we schedule the hands-on runbook session, below are the minimal preflight items our onboarding and ops teams need validated so we can finalize the activation window. I kept this tight to avoid surprises during the cutover.

Preflight checklist (please confirm or attach evidence):
- Network peering: VPC peering or TGW details (account IDs and CIDR ranges).
- Egress NAT: list of static egress IPs (or confirm use of managed NAT gateway) and port allowlist.
- Inbound rules: ports and source ranges for control plane and health checks.
- Service accounts: mapping of Redwood service accounts to Aldea IAM roles (CSV preferred).
- KMS access: KMS key ARNs and contact for KMS admin; confirm whether HSM is required.
- Certificate management: who will rotate TLS certs (Aldea or Redwood) and cert expiry policy.
- Throughput SLO: expected concurrent QPS for the initial 30-day ramp.
- Maintenance windows: preferred weekly and blackout windows for the first 90 days.

Attachments: rwd-network-diagram-v2.png (logical topology), sample service-account CSV (template).

Can you send the CIDR list and service-account mapping by end of day Monday so Marissa and I can pre-validate routing and IAM? If anything on the checklist is a no-go, flag it now and we’ll route to engineering.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Samir Khan <samir@aldea.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@aldea.health, procurement@aldea.health
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Edge connectivity preflight and ops checkpoints

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Quick answers and a couple questions below:

- CIDRs: attaching our perimeter ranges (private-ranges.txt) — note we have an internal overlay network from 10.40.0.0/16 for edge nodes.
- Egress: we plan to use a pool of 5 static NAT IPs initially; I’ll attach the list later today.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS (no HSM). KMS admin is Priya Shah (priya@aldea.health).
- Service accounts: we can populate the CSV — thanks for the template.
- Certs: Aldea prefers to manage cert rotation; we can share our rotation cadence.
- Throughput: initial QPS estimate is 150 concurrent requests, spiking to 400 during business hours.

A few clarifying questions:
1) For health checks, does Redwood require a public endpoint or can checks be performed via the peering connection?
2) For SOC2 evidence/attestations later, who should procurement loop in on your side?

I’ve copied procurement for the contract coordination; they may have a DocuSign rolling requirement.

Thanks,
Samir Khan
Head of Infrastructure — Aldea Health
samir@aldea.health

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge connectivity preflight and ops checkpoints

Samir — thanks for the quick reply and the overlay CIDR note. A couple of technical confirmations from the onboarding team:

- Health checks: we can perform health checks over the peering connection — public endpoints are not required for the control plane. We'll provide a short-lived connectivity test agent you can run on a bastion to validate routing.
- NAT IPs: 5 static NAT addresses is fine; please include reverse DNS entries if you have them.
- KMS: AWS KMS is supported; we’ll need a cross-account IAM role with kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt and an access policy that allows our service account to encrypt/decrypt with the specified key. Please use the attached template (aldea-service-account-mapping.csv) and populate Principal ARNs column.
- Throughput: 150–400 QPS is within our expected ramp; we’ll size initial pool conservatively and revisit after the first 30 days.

Action items we’ll take on immediately:
1) Marissa will run a routing validation against the overlay CIDRs after you send the NAT IPs (target: Mon 21 Sep).
2) Ben will confirm public IP allocation and update the SLO note.
3) Jordan will schedule the runbook walkthrough (30–45 min).

Attaching: aldea-service-account-mapping.csv (please populate and return). Linking JIRA ticket for orchestration: JIRA: OPS-4321.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@aldea.health>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge connectivity preflight and ops checkpoints

Adding a couple of operational notes from capacity and infra side:

- Certificate rotation: if Aldea manages certs, please ensure we have a documented process for emergency rotation and a reachable on-call during rotation windows. Automated cert push is supported but requires a short-lived service credential; see the CSV template for the scope.
- NAT & Egress: please confirm whether Aldea will use a single public ASN or multiple — this affects BGP translations and our egress mapping.
- Throughput SLO: we’ll provision initial workers for 200 QPS steady-state with burst capacity to 500 for the first 14 days, then re-evaluate telemetry. If you see higher sustained usage, open OPS-4321 and we’ll shift capacity.

One ask: procurement, if you foresee any SLA exceptions (credits, special uptime windows) please flag now so we can get leadership approval. For SOC2 evidence, loop in Kimberly (cc’d) — she’ll coordinate the artifact package and timelines.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior PM, Private Deployments
ben@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Edge connectivity preflight and ops checkpoints

Samir —

Thanks to you and your team for the fast responses. To summarize next steps and acceptance criteria before we move to the activation window:

Pre-activation acceptance (what we need from Aldea):
- Completed aldea-service-account-mapping.csv with Principal ARNs and delegated role names.
- List of 5 static egress IPs with reverse DNS and contact for NAT gateway owner.
- KMS cross-account role created and confirmed by Priya Shah (kms admin).
- Confirmed maintenance windows and blackout dates for the first 90 days.
- A primary on-call contact for cert rotation and a secondary for emergency access.

Planned on-call/runbook session: Wed 22 Sep 2026 10:00–10:45 PT; calendar invite to follow. During the runbook we will:
- Walk the network diagram and routing validation steps.
- Run the short-lived connectivity agent to validate peering.
- Validate service-account role assumptions and KMS permissions.
- Smoke test a controlled inference call and confirm telemetry.

If all items above are confirmed during the session we’ll proceed with a staged activation starting Thu 23 Sep with an initial ramp target of 200 QPS.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
